hints: Differentiate the square-root composite function using the chain rule.
At $x=\pi/4$, substitute $\tan x=1$ to verify the stated gradient.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $y = (\tan x)^{\frac{1}{2}}$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1}{2}(\tan x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\sec^2 x = \dfrac{\sec^2 x}{2\sqrt{\tan x}}$$

Express the derivative entirely in terms of $\tan x$ using $\sec^2 x = 1 + \tan^2 x$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1 + \tan^2 x}{2\sqrt{\tan x}}$$

Verify the derivative at $x = \dfrac{1}{4}\pi$ where $\tan\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\pi\right) = 1$:
$$\left.\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right|_{x=\pi/4} = \dfrac{1 + 1^2}{2\sqrt{1}} = \dfrac{2}{2} = 1$$
This confirms the given condition.

hints: Set the derivative from part (a) equal to $1$ at $x=a$ and let $t=\tan a$.
Square to obtain $(1+t^2)^2=4t$, expand the quartic, and factor out the known root $t=1$.
Divide by $t-1$ to obtain the required cubic factor.
walkthrough:
Set the derivative from part (a) equal to $1$ at $x = a$:
$$\dfrac{1 + \tan^2 a}{2\sqrt{\tan a}} = 1$$

Let $t = \tan a$ to express the equation in terms of $t$:
$$\dfrac{1 + t^2}{2\sqrt{t}} = 1$$
$$1 + t^2 = 2\sqrt{t}$$

Square both sides to eliminate the square root:
$$(1 + t^2)^2 = (2\sqrt{t})^2$$
$$1 + 2t^2 + t^4 = 4t$$
$$t^4 + 2t^2 - 4t + 1 = 0$$

Divide by the known factor $(t - 1)$ corresponding to the root $a = \dfrac{1}{4}\pi$ ($t = 1$):
$$(t^4 + 2t^2 - 4t + 1) \div (t - 1) = t^3 + t^2 + 3t - 1$$

Conclude the cubic equation for $t = \tan a$:
$$t^3 + t^2 + 3t - 1 = 0$$
This completes the proof.

hints: Apply the supplied iteration in radian mode, using each output as the next input.
Record every $a_n$ to 4 decimal places and continue until the values justify a single answer to 2 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Rearrange $t^3 + t^2 + 3t - 1 = 0$ to express $t = \tan a$:
$$3t = 1 - t^2 - t^3 \implies t = \dfrac{1}{3}(1 - t^2 - t^3)$$
$$a = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{3}(1 - \tan^2 a - \tan^3 a)\right)$$

Apply the iterative formula $a_{n+1} = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{3}(1 - \tan^2 a_n - \tan^3 a_n)\right)$ with an initial estimate, e.g. $a_1 = 0.3$:
$$a_2 = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{3}(1 - \tan^2(0.3) - \tan^3(0.3))\right) \approx 0.2854$$
$$a_3 = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{3}(1 - \tan^2(0.2854) - \tan^3(0.2854))\right) \approx 0.2894$$
$$a_4 = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{3}(1 - \tan^2(0.2894) - \tan^3(0.2894))\right) \approx 0.2883$$
$$a_5 = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{3}(1 - \tan^2(0.2883) - \tan^3(0.2883))\right) \approx 0.2886$$

Observe that iterates stabilize and round to $0.29$ to 2 decimal places.
(Checking interval $(0.285, 0.295)$: $g(0.285) < 0$ and $g(0.295) > 0$, verifying stability.)
Thus:
$$a = 0.29$$
